subject: CatalystRx privacy pledge confirmation & ops handoff
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@catalystrx.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@catalystrx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: privacy commitments from today's discovery call (next steps)

Hi Ethan / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment and can get procurement moving.

Recap from our call:
- You will not permit Redwood to use CatalystRx input data for model training or tuning (no LLM learning).
- Data residency requirement: all request/response logs and any persistent storage of customer artifacts must be kept in an EU region only.
- PII handling: you requested PII redaction at edge and that PII not be present in stored logs.
- Audit/log access: CatalystRx needs access to audit logs for compliance. We discussed a 90-day retention view for your SecOps team, after which logs are truncated/aggregated.

What I'm proposing as immediate next steps:
1) Attached: draft Data Handling Addendum (DDA) and our SOC 2 summary (attachment stubs below). Please review the DDA and flag any language you want changed.
2) If the DDA looks good, I'll generate a DocuSign envelope for countersignature and route to our Legal/Procurement.
3) To implement the EU residency requirement we need the target account region and the internal contact for your cloud/network team.
4) I'll loop in our Customer Reliability/OPS lead (Ben Carter) to confirm logging retention and the mechanism for encrypted EU storage.

A few quick notes on capabilities so expectations are clear:
- We enforce a contractual prohibition on model improvement from customer contents when DDA is in place. That prevents any training or tuning on your data.
- We offer configurable log retention per contract (30 / 90 / custom) along with a mode to pseudonymize or fully redact transcripts before storage.
- Audit logs can be provided as read-only S3 exports in an EU bucket under a customer-owned project if you prefer.

Attachments (sent as stubs):
- redwood_data_addendum_v1.pdf (DRAFT)
- SOC2-type2-summary.pdf

If you confirm the high level above I'll: 1) share an edited DDA with the clause you requested on explicit non-use for training, 2) open a HubSpot ticket and DocuSign envelope, and 3) send a short ops checklist for your SOC/infra team.

Cheers,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@catalystrx.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@catalystrx.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:21:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up: privacy commitments from today's discovery call (next steps)

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear note. Quick answers from our side: we confirm the following expectations that must be reflected in the DDA/contract:

- CatalystRx will not permit Redwood to use our data for model training or model improvement under any circumstances (we need explicit contractual language).
- All logs and retained artifacts must remain in the EU (we prefer Frankfurt region).
- PII: we need edge redaction enabled; anything that cannot be reliably redacted should not be stored.
- Audit/log retention: legal is pushing for a 90-day searchable retention window for investigation purposes; after 90 days we accept aggregated-only exports (no raw transcript retention).

Next steps from our side: I'll route the DDA to our Legal and Procurement for a quick read; procurement may ask for a short SOC/cert bundle for their checklist (SOC2 summary looks helpful). If you can provide a DocuSign link that will speed things up.

Also: can you confirm whether the logs we can access will contain raw user content or only metadata if we request the read-only S3 exports?

Priya
VP Security & Compliance
CatalystRx
priya.sharma@catalystrx.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@catalystrx.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@catalystrx.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 13:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: privacy commitments from today's discovery call (next steps)

Hi Priya — looping in ops to confirm specifics. Short answers below and implementation notes.

- Contractual prohibition: we will add explicit language to the DDA that Redwood will not use CatalystRx content for model training, evaluation, or reinforcement learning. Please review the forthcoming clause and suggest edits.
- EU residency: we support tenant-level region isolation. We can pin your account to eu-west (Frankfurt) and ensure storage and logs are kept in that region.
- PII redaction: we offer an edge redaction layer that can be configured to drop or pseudonymize detected PII before any telemetry leaves your environment. We'll share detection rules.
- Audit logs: when we provide read-only S3 exports in your EU bucket, those exports can be either raw (full transcripts) or redacted/metadata-only depending on the configuration you agree to in contract. From a compliance perspective, many customers take 90 days raw + long-term aggregated only.

Implementation steps for Redwood OPS (what we'll do):
1) Prepare a revised DDA with the "no-training" clause and explicit EU residency binding.
2) Prepare a DocuSign envelope and attach the SOC2 summary and DDA.
3) Provision a workspace in eu-west for CatalystRx and configure log retention to 90 days by default pending legal sign-off.
4) Provide a short technical ops checklist to your infra contact describing the S3 export process and encryption keys (we can support customer-managed keys).

I'm marking the HubSpot ticket and will follow up with timelines (expected: DDA revision + DocuSign within 48 business hours).

(Attachment references: redwood_data_addendum_v1.pdf — revised language forthcoming.)

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
